kept.title: Command Injection in Benchmarking Utility
kept.description: The `exec` function in `benchmarking/compare/index.js` at line 6 uses `execSync` to run shell commands derived directly from user-supplied branch names or arguments without sanitization.
steps_to_exploit: Invoke the benchmark with a malicious argument, e.g., 'main; rm -rf /'.
The script passes the unsanitized input to `execSync` via the checkout helper functions.
The shell executes the arbitrary command with the privileges of the Node.js process.
kept.impact: Full command execution on the host machine, potentially leading to unauthorized data access or system compromise.

kept.title: Unsafe Deserialization of Malformed Input
kept.description: The `unflatten` function in `src/parse.js` processes serialized data that can cause excessive memory allocation or stack depth when handling nested or sparse structures if inputs are carefully crafted.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a payload representing a deeply nested recursive object or a heavily fragmented array.
Submit the payload to the `devalue.parse()` function.
Observe high memory usage or heap exhaustion as the hydration routine recursively allocates memory.
kept.impact: Denial-of-service via resource exhaustion of the Node.js process.

kept.title: Arbitrary Code Execution via Function Constructor in Uneval
kept.description: The `uneval` function uses `Function` or `eval`-like patterns to generate JS code at line 526 in `src/uneval.js` without sufficient validation of the structure.
steps_to_exploit: Pass an object with malicious keys that override `toString` or prototype methods.
The `uneval` process generates a string representation including these malicious properties.
The recipient evaluating the string executes the injected code payloads.
kept.impact: Execution of arbitrary code on the client or server environment where the serialized output is processed.

kept.title: Path Traversal in Results Output
kept.description: The benchmarking script in `benchmarking/compare/index.js` writes results to paths constructed by joining a directory path and an unsanitized branch name at line 56.
steps_to_exploit: Pass a branch name containing directory traversal sequences, such as '../../etc/passwd'.
The script attempts to write a JSON file to the targeted directory.
Files on the filesystem may be overwritten or created in unintended locations.
kept.impact: Unauthorized file creation or potential overwrite of sensitive configuration files.

kept.title: Prototype Pollution via Object Deserialization
kept.description: The `unflatten` routine in `src/parse.js` handles object keys, and while it checks for `__proto__` at line 166, it may not adequately catch all variations of property assignment leading to pollution in specific JavaScript environments.
steps_to_exploit: Create a payload with a non-standard property name representing a prototype path if the input validation is bypassed.
Deserialize the object using `devalue.parse`.
The prototype is modified, affecting subsequent object instantiations.
kept.impact: Modification of global object behavior, potentially leading to privilege escalation or further injection attacks.

kept.title: Insecure Use of Native Syntax Flag
kept.description: The `package.json` suggests running benchmarks with `--allow-natives-syntax` at lines 35-36, which exposes V8 internal functions to user code.
steps_to_exploit: An attacker contributes a benchmark file containing arbitrary JS code using V8 internal APIs.
The CI pipeline runs the benchmark with the dangerous flag enabled.
V8 internal routines are used to manipulate heap memory or break sandbox boundaries.
kept.impact: Bypassing of engine-level protections and potential privilege escalation within the JS environment.

kept.title: Information Disclosure in Error Messages
kept.description: The `DevalueError` class stores the entire root object in the error instance at line 28 in `src/utils.js`, which may leak sensitive information when logged.
steps_to_exploit: Cause a stringify error on a large, sensitive object graph.
Catch the error and log it to an external observability tool.
Sensitive credentials or user data are exposed in the logs.
kept.impact: Exposure of PII or credentials through system logs.

kept.title: Weak Randomness in `get_name`
kept.description: The `get_name` function uses predictable character sequences at line 13 in `src/uneval.js` for variable naming during code generation.
steps_to_exploit: Reverse-engineer the naming algorithm.
Predict generated variable names for a known set of inputs.
Craft an input that conflicts with or shadows internal variable names in the generated `uneval` code.
kept.impact: Increased susceptibility to collision-based injection or logic errors.

kept.title: ReDoS in Regex Parsing
kept.description: The identifier regex `is_identifier` in `src/utils.js` (line 111) is potentially vulnerable to catastrophic backtracking when provided with extremely long strings.
steps_to_exploit: Provide a very long string as a property key during stringification.
The identifier test enters a high-complexity backtracking state.
The thread blocks, preventing further processing.

kept.title: Use of Deprecated/Legacy Runtimes
kept.description: The `encode_legacy` function uses `String.fromCharCode.apply` which is prone to stack overflow on very large binary arrays at line 37 in `src/base64.js`.
steps_to_exploit: Create a very large `ArrayBuffer` and attempt to serialize it.
The runtime attempts to pass a massive number of arguments to `String.fromCharCode`.
The script crashes due to call stack limits.

kept.title: Insecure Timing Sensitivity
kept.description: The `track` function in `benchmarking/utils.js` (line 6) uses `setTimeout` to wait for cleanup, which is non-deterministic and can be affected by environment load.
steps_to_exploit: Manipulate system load to interfere with garbage collection events.
Force inaccurate benchmarking results which might lead developers to select suboptimal or insecure algorithms.
The resulting performance data is unreliable.
kept.impact: Reduced accuracy of performance metrics; unreliable security testing.

kept.title: Missing Error Handling in Directory Creation
kept.description: The `mkdirSync` call in `benchmarking/compare/index.js` uses an empty `catch` block (line 60), potentially masking filesystem permission issues or underlying race conditions.
steps_to_exploit: Run the benchmark in a directory with restricted write permissions.
The `mkdirSync` fails silently.
Subsequent writes fail, leading to unexpected application state.
kept.impact: Instability and unpredictable behavior under constrained environments.

kept.title: Reliance on Global Constructor References
kept.description: The `fromViewInfo` function at line 144 in `src/operations.js` pulls constructors directly from `globalThis` based on user-provided strings.
steps_to_exploit: Identify accessible constructors on `globalThis` that should not be used for serialization.
Craft a serialized object with a 'tag' that references one of these dangerous constructors.
The deserializer instantiates an object that could have unexpected side effects.
kept.impact: Potential for unauthorized instantiation of sensitive objects.

kept.title: Overly Permissive Prettier Config
kept.description: The `.prettierrc` file contains an override that disables formatting for `test-results/**` (line 8), potentially allowing unformatted, malicious code to be committed to the repo undetected.
steps_to_exploit: Submit a pull request containing malicious code within the `test-results` folder.
The CI/Prettier checks are bypassed for those files.
The malicious code is merged into the codebase.
kept.impact: Maintenance of potentially compromised test infrastructure or malicious files.

kept.title: Incomplete Validation of `ArrayBuffer` Encoding
kept.description: The `unflatten` logic handles `ArrayBuffer` but only performs basic checks, possibly allowing non-base64 strings to crash the base64 decoder in `src/parse.js` line 206.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a serialized object with an `ArrayBuffer` type but a non-string or corrupted base64 value.
Deserializer calls `decode64` with invalid input.
The application throws an unhandled exception.
kept.impact: Denial-of-service via unhandled exceptions in the parsing routine.
